fields.AN_Notes: Theoretical essay that proposes hermeneutic reverse engineering (Balsamo 2011) to examine data and algorithmic bias in AI systems, framed by boundary objects and intersectional feminist thought. AN_Bias_Axes: race and gender are coded from the essay's own sentences that develop the face-detection example (light skin as the norm, 'societal definitions of race and gender'); the opening list of race, gender, ability, language, class, economic background and religion is an enumeration. Sexual_Orientation_Identity is not coded, because gender identity appears only in the single cited Keyes (2018) sentence on automatic gender recognition, which the essay reports and does not develop. Intersectional is not coded, no passage makes an outcome depend on a combination of axes. AN_Harm_Types: Exclusionary_Norms from the essay's own argument on exclusion through hegemonic narration and light skin as the norm, and from its conclusion on questioning what is normal and who falls outside; Erasure from its own finding that questioning data reveals whose cultural narrative is missing. The cited cases of Buolamwini, Noble and Gebru are not coded as harm types. AN_Mitigation_Stage Organisational_Process and AN_Mitigation_Status Proposed: participatory co-design workshops and actionable AI audits are research perspectives, nothing is demonstrated or evaluated. AN_Gender_Understanding Unclear and AN_Gender_Definition Absent: the essay states no understanding of gender of its own; the phrase 'societal definitions of race and gender' attributes the categories to the training of a face-detection system within a cited case and does not state that gender is socially produced, so the Social_Construct threshold of codebook 1.4.1 is not met. AN_Prompting_Role None: observing outputs for different prompts appears once as a cited interrogation idea. AN_Task None: AI is the object of critique, no professional task of AI use is described.

fields.AN_Notes: UNESCO reference framework of twelve AI competency blocks for school students (four aspects by three progression levels) with curricular goals, pedagogical methods, learning environments and assessment items. Inclusivity is one of five key principles with its own section (2.4), hence Diversitaet ja. Bias enters as the non-discrimination principle, as anti-bias measures within section 2.4, the data biases lab and the competency to critique AI-amplified biases; it recurs as learning content beside privacy, human agency and environmental sustainability and is not the framework's central contribution, hence Bias_Ungleichheit teilweise. AN_Bias_Axes None: gender, ethnicity, culture, ability, socio-economic status and language appear only in enumerations of bias types or disaggregation variables. AN_Harm_Types None: no harm mechanism is established for the framework's own object. AN_Mitigation_Stage: Pre_Processing (representative data, data engineering to remove identifiable biases in the data biases lab), In_Training (anti-discrimination and discrimination-free training methods), Organisational_Process (public validation before recommending AI tools, inclusive testing and auditing); all are recommended as curricular content or policy, hence Proposed. AN_Bias_Definition Implicit_Only. AN_Gender_Definition and AN_Gender_Understanding Not_Applicable: gender occurs only in enumerations. AN_Population Not_SW_Specific: school students in general education. AN_Task None: AI is the learning object of a school curriculum; students' own use of AI tools to practise writing is learning activity, not a task of professional practice, and AI-supported assessment by teachers appears only as a supplementary outlook in section 5.8. School teaching lies outside Teaching_Further_Education, which addresses professionals. AN_Prompting_Role None: prompts appear only in a privacy assessment item.

fields.AN_Notes: Survey of bias evaluation metrics, evaluation datasets and mitigation techniques for LLMs with three taxonomies and a harm taxonomy (Table 1). AN_Harm_Types: all nine values structure the survey's own synthesis as rows of Table 1 (representational harms and allocational harms) and, for six of them, as coded columns of Table 4; the Derogatory_Language row label is lost in the conversion of Table 1, so its passage comes from section 2.4.2. AN_Bias_Axes: coded from the targeted-social-group columns of Table 4 (age, gender identity, nationality, physical appearance, race, religion, sexual orientation) and from dialect as the survey's own worked example (African-American English, linguistic profiling); disability and socioeconomic status appear only in dataset enumerations and the 'Other' footnote and are not coded. Intersectional is not coded: the survey argues that group fairness can hold for each group while failing for intersectional subgroups, but names no axis combination whose result it develops. AN_Prompting_Role Research_Instrument: prompt datasets (sentence completions, question answering) are a class of the evaluation taxonomy; modified prompting language is reviewed as a mitigation technique, not recommended. AN_Prompt_Techniques General_Guidance, concrete strategy as synthesised: 'prompting language with different levels of abstraction to instruct the model to avoid using stereotypes' and prepending positive adjectives or phrases to a prompt (section 5.1.4). AN_Mitigation_Stage: the four technical stages are the survey's own taxonomy; Prompt_Practice from modified prompting language; Organisational_Process from participatory research designs, reporting standards and data governance proposed in section 6. AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated as a synthesised evaluation, not the survey's own experiment: the survey reports that Borchers et al. (2022) found instructions prompting diversity or gender equality unsuccessful for bias removal, and that pruning 10-20% of parameters increased resistance to jailbreaking (Hasan, Rugina and Wang 2024); other techniques are inventoried without assessment. AN_Gender_Understanding Social_Construct: the survey states that social groups, which by Definition 3 include gender identity and sex, are socially constructed, contested and tied to power imbalances, and it adopts the critique that binary and immutable gender modelling erases trans, nonbinary and intersex people; its own Figure 1 example uses a male and female substitution. AN_Gender_Definition Implicit_Only because gender itself is not defined. AN_Task None: general LLM bias survey without an application task.

fields.AN_Notes: Survey of bias evaluation metrics, evaluation datasets and mitigation techniques for LLMs with three taxonomies and a harm taxonomy (Table 1). AN_Harm_Types: all nine values structure the survey's own synthesis as rows of Table 1 (representational harms and allocational harms) and, for six of them, as coded columns of Table 4; the Derogatory_Language row label is lost in the conversion of Table 1, so its passage comes from section 2.4.2. AN_Bias_Axes: coded from the targeted-social-group columns of Table 4 (age, gender identity, nationality, physical appearance, race, religion, sexual orientation) and from dialect as the survey's own worked example (African-American English, linguistic profiling); disability and socioeconomic status appear only in dataset enumerations and the 'Other' footnote and are not coded. Intersectional is not coded: the survey argues that group fairness can hold for each group while failing for intersectional subgroups, but names no axis combination whose result it develops. AN_Prompting_Role Research_Instrument: prompt datasets (sentence completions, question answering) are a class of the evaluation taxonomy; modified prompting language is reviewed as a mitigation technique, not recommended. AN_Prompt_Techniques General_Guidance, concrete strategy as synthesised: 'prompting language with different levels of abstraction to instruct the model to avoid using stereotypes' and prepending positive adjectives or phrases to a prompt (section 5.1.4). AN_Mitigation_Stage: the four technical stages are the survey's own taxonomy; Prompt_Practice from modified prompting language; Organisational_Process from participatory research designs, reporting standards and data governance proposed in section 6. AN_Mitigation_Status Evaluated as a synthesised evaluation, not the survey's own experiment: the survey reports that Borchers et al. (2022) found instructions prompting diversity or gender equality unsuccessful for bias removal, and that pruning 10-20% of parameters increased resistance to jailbreaking (Hasan, Rugina and Wang 2024); other techniques are inventoried without assessment. AN_Gender_Understanding Social_Construct: the survey states that social groups, which by Definition 3 include gender identity and sex, are socially constructed, contested and tied to power imbalances, and it adopts the critique that binary and immutable gender modelling erases trans, nonbinary and intersex people; its own Figure 1 example uses a male and female substitution. AN_Gender_Definition Implicit_Only because gender itself is not defined. AN_Task None: general LLM bias survey without an application task.
